title: The evolution of insect visual opsin genes with specific consideration of the influence of ocelli and life history traits
why: Tremex, receptor_classes: a survey of the visual opsin genes of insects (the long-, short- and ultraviolet-wavelength groups and the LW2a and LW2b duplication), listed in this harvest's Siricidae vision review. The stored abstract stops before its species, and main's sweep-42 record (Diapheromera) reports that the species list sits in its Additional file 1, which no reader has opened, so a Tremex species may be among the insects whose opsin genes it counts (an intact opsin gene predicts a receptor class and does not measure one). It is outside the canon file, so receptor_classes stays out of this unit's Tremex records. The desk's web pair for the trait ("Tremex spectral sensitivity" and "pigeon tremex spectral sensitivity") returned patents, cichlid and electroretinogram method papers, a Durham thesis and other studies of pigeon colour vision, and no horntail. Title, year, journal and DOI from the harvest output; not opened.
get: open access (gold, cc-by per OpenAlex): https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1186/s12862-022-01960-8.pdf ; the species list is in Additional file 1

title: USE OF MOLECULAR TECHNIQUES TO ADDRESS THE EVOLUTION OF DISPLAY TRAITS IN THE PTILONORHYNCHIDAE AND OTHER PASSERIFORM SPECIES
journal: University of Maryland (thesis; University Libraries repository)
why: Cormobates leucophaea, lambda_max_nm and spectral_range_nm: the one hit of the harvest query "Cormobates spectral sensitivity opsin" (it also came back for "Cormobates vision" and "Cormobates visual field"), so its text names Cormobates beside opsin or spectral-sensitivity words. The stored abstract describes molecular work on the evolution of display traits in bowerbirds and other passerines, so the thesis may give an SWS1 opsin sequence, and so the predicted violet- or ultraviolet-sensitive type, for the white-throated treecreeper (an opsin sequence predicts a pigment class and does not measure a peak). Main holds the published bowerbird pigment paper (Coyle et al. 2012, J Exp Biol) for the satin bowerbird only, through a 2012 Coyle dissertation on DRUM, and the compiled SWS1 file of Odeen and Hastad 2013 with no treecreeper. The desk's web pair for the traits ("Cormobates spectral sensitivity" and "white-throated treecreeper spectral sensitivity") returned an insect colour-vision review, cichlid and Drosophila papers, patents, untitled repository records and species pages for the bird, and no treecreeper pigment. Title and year from the harvest output (it gives no DOI); not opened.
get: thesis, open in the University of Maryland repository (green per OpenAlex): http://hdl.handle.net/1903/9510

title: Morphological traits of the eyes of Lepidoptera indicate selection for binocular vision in both diurnal butterflies and nocturnal moths
why: acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg of Machimia: an eye-model study of 2,730 specimens of 224 butterfly and moth species "widely sampled across a tribal level phylogeny of butterflies and a recent genomic sampling of moths" (stored abstract; the harvest lists it under the Lycaena genus queries and the Hesperiidae and Riodinidae family reviews), whose species table main has not read (main's oa-12 logs 10 rows over 6 taxa from its text, none an acuity or interommatidial value), so a species of these genera may be among them. It is outside the canon file, so these traits stay out of this unit's search records, as the desk held the Lepidoptera acuity cells of harvest-43 on the same work. The desk's acuity web pairs for these genera returned no study of their eyes: "Machimia visual acuity" returned human acuity pages, patents, a visual-prosthesis preprint and a dictionary entry, and "gold-striped leaftier visual acuity" returned species pages for the moth (Wikipedia, Earth.com, Butterflies and Moths of North America, worldspecies), news stories on animal acuity, the Purdue copy of a bird retina paper and two Ikiam records of a study of acuity in Heliconius butterflies. Title, year and DOI from the harvest output; authors left empty; not opened.
